facts.fact_text: On 26 March 2017, the applicant held a meeting at the specially designated location for public events in Krylya Sovetov Park.
According to the applicant, about 1,500 people attended the meeting held in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017.
According to the applicant, the meeting held in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017 lasted for about one hour and twenty minutes.
According to the Government, about 400 people participated in the meeting held in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017.
According to the Government, during the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017, the police used loudspeakers to order the participants to disperse.
According to the applicant, no announcements were made through loudspeakers during the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017.
According to the applicant, a police officer approached her during the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017 and demanded that she stop the unlawful public event.
According to the applicant, she replied to the police officer's demand by referring to the Vakhitovskiy District Court's decision of 24 March 2017 and stating that the meeting was lawful.

In the VKontakte message of 23 March 2017, the applicant stated that people were entitled to assemble peacefully and that it had therefore been decided to hold a meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park at 2 p.m. on 26 March 2017 to protest against corruption.
On 16 March 2017, the Kazan Town Administration refused to approve the meeting notified by the applicant on 14 March 2017.
The Kazan Town Administration's refusal of 16 March 2017 was based on the claim that other (unspecified) public events were scheduled at the locations chosen by the applicant at the same time.
On 22 March 2017, the applicant accepted the venue proposed by the Kazan Town Administration for the "picket".
On 23 March 2017, the applicant published a message on VKontakte criticising the Kazan Town Administration for its decision not to allow the meeting.

On 24 March 2017, the Kazan department of internal affairs warned the applicant that if she held a public event at one of the locations indicated in her notifications of 14 and 17 March 2017, she would be held liable.
According to the Government, during the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017, the police used loudspeakers to order the participants to disperse.
According to the applicant, a police officer approached her during the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017 and demanded that she stop the unlawful public event.
The applicant was arrested on her way home after the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park at about 4.20 p.m. on 26 March 2017.
The police immediately drew up a report stating that the applicant had been escorted to the police station so that a report on an administrative offence could be drawn up.

An arrest record drawn up at the same time as the escort report stated that the applicant had been arrested "in connection with an administrative offence [sic.] under Articles 20.2 § 2 [and] 19.3 § 1 [of the Code of Administrative Offences] for examination of the case".
At 6 p.m. on 26 March 2017, the police drew up a report on an administrative offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences against the applicant.
In the report under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the police noted that the applicant had organised an unauthorised public event.

In the report under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the police noted that the applicant had published a message on VKontakte calling for participation in the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017.

In the report under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the police noted that the applicant had held a meeting from 2 to 3 p.m. on 26 March 2017 in which about 400 people had participated.

In the report under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the police noted that the applicant had notified the Kazan Town Administration of her intention to hold a meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park but that the town administration had refused to allow the meeting.
In the report under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the police noted that the applicant had been allowed to hold a "picket" at another location.

In the report under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the police stated that by holding an unauthorised meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park, the applicant had breached the requirements of section 4 paragraphs 4 and 5 of the Public Assemblies Act and had thereby committed an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
At 6 p.m. on 26 March 2017, the police also drew up a report on an administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences against the applicant.

The report on the administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences added that the applicant had been warned by the Kazan department of internal affairs that she would be held liable if she went ahead with a public event at a location which had not been approved by the Kazan Town Administration.

The report on the administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences stated that the police had ordered the applicant to stop the meeting but she had not taken any actions to comply with that order, and that the meeting had lasted until about 3 p.m.

The report on the administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences stated that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order of the police and had thereby committed an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

On 27 March 2017, the Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan, in two separate judgments, found the applicant guilty of offences under Articles 19.3 and 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan found that the applicant had organised an unauthorised public event, including by publishing a message on VKontakte calling for participation.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan found that the applicant had refused to obey a lawful order given by the police to stop the unauthorised public event.

The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan noted that the applicant had notified the Kazan Town Administration of her intention to hold a meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park but that the town administration had refused to allow the meeting and had proposed that she hold a "picket" at another location.

The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan noted that the applicant had been warned by the Kazan department of internal affairs that she would be held liable if she went ahead with the public event at locations which had not been approved by the Kazan Town Administration.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan noted that the applicant had held the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park despite the warning from the Kazan department of internal affairs.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan noted that the police had ordered the applicant to stop the meeting but she had not complied with that order.

The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan did not reply to the applicant's argument that the Kazan Town Administration's decision of 16 March 2017 refusing to approve the meeting had been annulled on judicial review and that the meeting had therefore to be considered as authorised and lawful, and the police's order to stop it unlawful.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan sentenced the applicant to a fine of 1,000 Russian roubles under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan sentenced the applicant to twenty hours of community work under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

On 17 May 2017, the Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic upheld both judgments of 27 March 2017 of the Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan on appeal, finding them lawful, well reasoned and justified.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the applicant's and her counsel's arguments that she was innocent and had been unlawfully charged under Articles 19.3 and 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences were unsubstantiated and based on an incorrect interpretation of the applicable legal provisions and an incorrect assessment of the facts.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the evidence cumulatively showed that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order by a police officer who was fulfilling his duty to safeguard public order and ensure public safety.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic concluded that the organiser of the public event had not fully complied with the procedure for organising and holding public events, which rendered the public event unlawful.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the judicial decision finding the Kazan Town Administration's failure to act unlawful did not amount to an unconditional approval of the location and time of the public event and did not exempt the organiser from fulfilling the obligations imposed by the Public Events Act.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the judicial decision finding the Kazan Town Administration's failure to act unlawful did not transform an unauthorised public event into an authorised one.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the police officer acted within the powers provided by law with the aim of fulfilling his duty to ensure public safety and order, and that his order to stop the public event addressed to its organiser could be considered lawful in accordance with the Police Act.

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that the public authority may propose a change of location or time of a public event to be held at a specially designated location and not requiring notification only if another public event has been scheduled to take place at the same location and time and either (i) the number of participants of the two simultaneous events will exceed the maximum capacity of the location, or (ii) it will not be possible to ensure the peaceful character of the simultaneous events by applying security arrangements habitually used at public events with a comparable number of participants (point 15).

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that a cultural event, a fair or some other mass event not falling under the Public Events Act, scheduled to take place at the same specially designated location at the same time, may not in itself serve as lawful grounds for proposing to change the location or time of a public event (point 16).

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that a cultural event, a fair or other mass event not falling under the Public Events Act may serve as lawful grounds for proposing to change the location or time of a public event only if information about that mass event was duly published and it will not be possible to ensure safety at the two events if they are held simultaneously (point 16).
